Marketing · Rednote account

A local's food & grad-life diary

A personal account I taught myself to run while studying in Macau: restaurant finds and grad-life plogs, told from a local, off-the-beaten-path angle. It became my training ground for content marketing.

29.7Klikes & saves

What it shows about my marketing

  1. Clear positioningA local insider plus grad-student life: a niche that set the account apart from generic food reviews.
  2. Consistent brandingThe same cover style and title format on every post, so readers know it's mine at a glance.
  3. Series contentA numbered “Macau grad-life plog” series that gave followers a reason to come back.
  4. Save-worthy valueThe top note was saved 701 times, more than it was liked, and shared 394 times: useful content travels.
04 · Brand Story Engine
AI workflow · Claude

One name, three files

A Claude workflow that turns one brand name into a cited research report, a newsletter article and a designed HTML article page. I wrote and tested every prompt on Ole Henriksen, turned the prompts into three skills, chained them into one loop, then ran the loop on Glossier to check it holds up on a second brand.

tools
Claude: prompts, skills, a master loop
my part
workflow design, prompts & quality rules
tested on
Ole Henriksen, Glossier
  1. step 1PromptsWrote each job as one detailed prompt and tested it by hand on Ole Henriksen.
  2. step 2SkillsSaved the three tested prompts as reusable Claude skills.
  3. step 3LoopBuilt one master skill that runs all three in order, with a quality check after each.
  4. step 4Re-testRan the full loop on Glossier to confirm it works on a brand it was not built on.
  5. step 5 · designedRoutineA scheduled task to run the loop on Mondays at 9:00. Designed, not yet set up.
The skills I made
  • brand-researchA cited report on any consumer brand: history, founder, positioning, channels, revenue, social marketing and takeaways. Figures that are not public are marked as such, never estimated.
  • brand-newsletter-articleTurns the report into an article of about 900 words in the style of 2 to 3 reference articles: hook, brand story, social strategy, takeaways (10 / 40 / 40 / 10), with numbered image markers.
  • brand-article-html-pageDesigns the article as one responsive HTML page in the style of 1 to 3 reference designs, with labelled image placeholders.
  • brand-story-loopThe master skill. One message, “Run brand-story-loop for [brand]”, runs all three in order and stops to ask if a check fails.
Rules I built in
  • Nothing is published. Every run ends with plain files for a person to review.
  • No guessing. Every claim is cited; company-reported claims are labelled and conflicting sources are reported side by side.
  • A check after every step. Sources, structure and length are verified; failures are fixed for up to two rounds, then the loop stops and asks.
  • The page is tested. It is rendered at desktop and phone width and checked for overlaps before delivery.

From Asia to the Nordics, each step grew out of curiosity about people, places and how they connect.

I have always loved European history, architecture and landscapes, and I plan my own routes when I travel. The same curiosity shaped my studies: three degrees with one question running through them, how people and systems connect across borders.
